title: Why does one line in this chapter refuse to repeat?

beats.narration: This chapter repeats itself word for word — except once. Can you hear the change?
The lines addressed to the other side are a frozen refrain: verse three and verse five are the identical sentence, repeated letter for letter. But the speaker's own lines refuse to hold still.

First: I do not serve what you serve — present tense, this moment. Then the line that breaks the symmetry: nor am I one who serves what you HAVE served — reaching back across the whole past. Their posture is photographed twice, unchanged. His denial moves through time.

One side is pinned to a single unchanging stance. The other side's refusal covers the present and the entire settled past. By the last verse — to you your way, to me mine — the separation is already total. Grammar sealed it.
